instruction: Check my internet connection speed using speedtest.net. Once the speed test is complete, extract the measurement results from speedtest.net/results and persist them to ~/Test/Speed/results.txt (creating directories along the path as required). Use this format: each metric on a distinct line with the metric name and its value separated by one space character.

metadata.explanation: Task requires executing an internet speed check through speedtest.net, retrieving measurements from speedtest.net/results, and writing to a file. Evaluator checks that the file contains three fundamental network statistics: Ping, Download, and Upload. This is a paraphrased version of the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator uses 'file_contains' which only checks for substring presence of 'Ping', 'Download', and 'Upload' anywhere in the file
Instruction explicitly requires a specific format: 'each metric on a distinct line with the metric name and its value separated by one space character'
The evaluator does NOT verify that metrics are on separate lines
The evaluator does NOT verify that metric names and values are separated by exactly one space
The evaluator does NOT verify the line-based format structure
File could contain 'PingDownloadUpload' all on one line or scattered in random text and still pass
Incomplete coverage: evaluator verifies file existence and keyword presence but ignores the critical format requirement
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Replace 'file_contains' with 'check_list' metric which supports regex patterns to verify line-based format
Use expected patterns like: ['^Ping\s+\S+', '^Download\s+\S+', '^Upload\s+\S+'] to ensure each metric appears at line start with a value
Alternative: Create a custom metric that parses the file line-by-line and validates the format: metric_name <single space> numeric_value
Ensure the metric checks that each required metric (Ping/Download/Upload) appears exactly once on its own line with proper spacing
